It defines the chosen one-particle Hilbert/Fock construction, continuous test-function smearing map with K(Pf)=0, induced Fock commutator, state functional, and conformal null-infinity/incoming-frequency-vacuum conventions. On each compact positive-frequency band it defines the bounded packet forms, direct-integral signal/environment number form, passive packet map, and exact operator-norm convergence premise. The four-dimensional identification with the one-dimensional exponential current and scattering assumptions remain explicitly adopted, not derived. Alpha corrected the state domain to the algebra generated by incoming annihilators, smeared fields and outgoing packet operators together with their adjoints, all on D_fin. Packet annihilators are conjugate-linear; B(f,g)=varpi(a_out(g)^*a_out(f)) has the declared conjugate-linear-first convention. Existence and the moment bounds remain explicit adopted premises.

Two nonzero future-null cotangent vectors $(p,\xi)$ and $(q,\zeta)$ are related, written $(p,\xi)\sim(q,\zeta)$, if $p=q$ and $\zeta=\xi$, or if there are a nonconstant future-directed affinely parametrized null geodesic $\gamma:I\to M$, parameters $s,t\in I$ in either order, and a common scale $\lambda>0$ such that
$$p=\gamma(s),\qquad q=\gamma(t),\qquad \xi=\lambda g_p(\dot\gamma(s),\cdot),\qquad \zeta=\lambda g_q(\dot\gamma(t),\cdot).$$

citations.quote: In the adopted frequency-diagonal Fock interpretation, the positive-frequency Fourier coefficient of the ordered current two-point function is $\omega/2$ times the mode occupation. Thus the occupation associated with spectral coefficient $S_k(\omega)$ is, by this model's normalization, $2S_k(\omega)/\omega$ for $\omega>0$. This identification is part of the adopted channel model; it is not a detector response or an observed particle count.

Put $\theta:=2\pi/k$ seconds and $n_\theta(\omega):=(e^{\theta\omega}-1)^{-1}$. Define the incoming number form on $\mathcal H_K\oplus\mathcal H_K$ by
$$q_{\ell,K}((f_1,f_2),(g_1,g_2)):=\int_K\overline{f_1(\omega)}g_1(\omega)n_\theta(\omega)\,d\omega,$$
where the first component is the near-horizon signal and the second is the independent incoming vacuum channel. Define the packet map induced by the first row of the passive mode transformation by
$$J_{\ell,K}f:=\bigl(\sqrt{\Gamma_\ell}\,f,\sqrt{1-\Gamma_\ell}\,f\bigr).$$
The exact limiting form is the adopted direct-integral model input
$$B_{\ell,\infty}(f,g):=q_{\ell,K}(J_{\ell,K}f,J_{\ell,K}g)=\int_K\overline{f(\omega)}g(\omega)\Gamma_\ell(\omega)n_\theta(\omega)\,d\omega.$$
Thus the signal has the exponential-channel occupation $n_\theta$, the environment and signal-environment cross terms vanish by the incoming vacuum and independence premises, and the passive map supplies the transmission factor. Assume that for each fixed $K$ the bounded forms converge in operator norm as $s\to+\infty$ to this $B_{\ell,\infty}$, meaning
$$\sup_{\|f\|_2,\|g\|_2\le1}|B_{\ell,s}(f,g)-B_{\ell,\infty}(f,g)|\longrightarrow0.$$

In the channel defined above, let $s=u-v$ and let $\omega$ be angular frequency in seconds$^{-1}$. Its two-point distribution in centered time is
$$C_k(s)=-\frac{k^2}{16\pi}\operatorname{csch}^2\left(\frac{k}{2}(s-i0)\right).$$
Its Fourier spectrum, using $\widehat C_k(\omega)=\int_{\mathbb R}C_k(s)e^{-i\omega s}\,ds$ in the distributional sense, is
$$S_k(\omega)=\frac{\omega}{2(e^{2\pi\omega/k}-1)}\quad(\omega\ne0),\qquad S_k(0)=\frac{k}{4\pi}.$$
Thus the precise detailed-balance relation at strip width $\theta=2\pi/k$ seconds is $S_k(-\omega)=e^{\theta\omega}S_k(\omega)$ for every $\omega>0$. No measured temperature is assigned.

Separately, for each fixed $\omega>0$, give $\mathbb C$ the second-variable-linear Hilbert inner product $\langle z,w\rangle_{\mathbb C}=\bar z w$, so $1\in\mathbb C$ is a unit vector, and put $\mathcal F=\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)$. Write $|m\rangle$ for the normalized vector in its $m$-particle sector, with $|0\rangle=\Omega$; the annihilation map satisfies $a_{\mathbb C}(1)|m\rangle=\sqrt m\,|m-1\rangle$ on finite-particle vectors. Its maximal closed domain is
$$D(a_{\mathbb C}(1))=\left\{\sum_{m\ge0}\psi_m|m\rangle:\sum_{m\ge0}m|\psi_m|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
Let $\Gamma:(0,\infty)\to[0,1]$ be any pointwise transmissivity function; no measurability is needed because every assertion below is mode-by-mode. Every square root below denotes the unique nonnegative real square root, which exists for each nonnegative argument in the usual Dedekind-complete ordered field $\mathbb R$. Let $\mathcal H=\mathcal F\widehat\otimes\mathcal F$ with product basis $|m,n\rangle=|m\rangle\otimes|n\rangle$. The tensor-factor annihilation operators $a=a_{\mathbb C}(1)\otimes I$ and $e=I\otimes a_{\mathbb C}(1)$ act on basis vectors by $a|m,n\rangle=\sqrt m\,|m-1,n\rangle$ and $e|m,n\rangle=\sqrt n\,|m,n-1\rangle$, with a zero result when the corresponding index is zero, and have domains
$$D(a)=\left\{\sum_{m,n\ge0}c_{mn}|m,n\rangle:\sum_{m,n\ge0}m|c_{mn}|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad D(e)=\left\{\sum_{m,n\ge0}c_{mn}|m,n\rangle:\sum_{m,n\ge0}n|c_{mn}|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
On their common domain $D:=D(a)\cap D(e)$ define, for each $\omega$, the two output operators by the following linear transformation, with $D(b_\omega)=D(d_\omega)=D$:
$$b_\omega=\sqrt{\Gamma(\omega)}\,a+\sqrt{1-\Gamma(\omega)}\,e.$$
The complementary output is $d_\omega=-\sqrt{1-\Gamma(\omega)}\,a+\sqrt{\Gamma(\omega)}\,e$, also defined on $D$. Let $\mathscr D_{\rm fin}=\operatorname{span}\{|m,n\rangle:m,n\in\mathbb N_0\}$ be the algebraic finite-particle subspace. It is contained in $D$ and invariant under $a,e$ and their creation operators; on it define $b_\omega^\dagger=\sqrt{\Gamma(\omega)}\,a^\dagger+\sqrt{1-\Gamma(\omega)}\,e^\dagger$ and $d_\omega^\dagger=-\sqrt{1-\Gamma(\omega)}\,a^\dagger+\sqrt{\Gamma(\omega)}\,e^\dagger$ as the corresponding creation combinations. Let $\psi_\omega\in D(a_{\mathbb C}(1))$ be a normalized signal vector and put the environment in its unit vacuum vector $\Omega_e=|0\rangle$. Then $\Psi_\omega:=\psi_\omega\otimes\Omega_e$ lies in $D$: if $\psi_\omega=\sum_m\psi_m|m\rangle$, the $a$-domain sum is $\sum_m m|\psi_m|^2<\infty$ and the $e$-domain sum is zero. Put $n_\omega=\|a_{\mathbb C}(1)\psi_\omega\|^2<\infty$ and define the output occupation by the quadratic form $\mathfrak n_{\rm out}(\omega):=\|b_\omega\Psi_\omega\|^2$. Then $\mathfrak n_{\rm out}(\omega)=\Gamma(\omega)n_\omega$. For the Planck occupation function $n_\theta(\omega)=(\exp(\theta\omega)-1)^{-1}$ with width $\theta>0$ measured in seconds, one has $n_\theta(\omega)>0$ for every $\omega>0$. Consequently, a filter preserving this same width at every positive frequency must satisfy $\Gamma(\omega)n_\theta(\omega)=n_\theta(\omega)$ and hence $\Gamma(\omega)=1$ at every $\omega$. derivations.claim: Fix $\ell$ and a normalized $f$ supported in $K$. The postulate identifies the near-horizon occupation with $2S_k(\omega)/\omega$; by [F1] and $\theta=2\pi/k$, this is $n_\theta(\omega)$. Work with the joint incoming number quadratic form supplied by the direct-integral Fock channel in [A2]. Write $q_K$ for its conjugate-linear-first, linear-second polarization on $\mathcal H_K\oplus\mathcal H_K$, with the first summand the signal and the second the incoming vacuum; its diagonal is the adopted input occupation. The frequency-diagonal signal form is $q_K((g,0),(h,0))=\int_K\overline{g(\omega)}h(\omega)n_\theta(\omega)d\omega$. It is bounded, since $n_\theta$ is continuous and bounded on the compact positive-frequency band $K$. The vacuum condition gives $q_K((0,h),(0,h))=0$. These are the quadratic-moment data of the two input channels already adopted in [A2]; they require neither a pure signal vector nor a normal density-matrix representation, and no assertion that a monochromatic annihilator belongs to the compactly smeared field algebra is used. To see that there is no additional cross-moment assumption, put $F=(g,0)$ and $E=(0,h)$. Positivity and sesquilinearity give $0\le q_K(F+zE,F+zE)=q_K(F,F)+2\operatorname{Re}(zq_K(F,E))$ for every $z\in\mathbb C$. Unless $q_K(F,E)=0$, a suitable phase and arbitrarily large modulus of $z$ make this negative. Hence both cross pairings vanish. In quadratic-moment Hilbert-space language, quotienting the input form by its null vectors and completing sends every vacuum annihilation label $E$ to the zero vector; its pairing with every finite signal annihilation image is therefore zero. Thus all cross pairings are fixed by positivity, with no operator product-domain or extra finite-cross-moment axiom. The passive map in [A2], with the same real coefficients as [F2], sends the output packet label to $J_\ell f=(\sqrt{\Gamma_\ell}\,f,\sqrt{1-\Gamma_\ell}\,f)$. The coefficients are bounded measurable functions on $K$, so $J_\ell$ is defined on $\mathcal H_K$ and $\|J_\ell f\|^2=\|f\|^2$. Pulling back the adopted input number form gives $B_{\ell,\infty}(f,f)=q_K(J_\ell f,J_\ell f)=\int_K|f(\omega)|^2\Gamma_\ell(\omega)n_\theta(\omega)d\omega$. This calculates the diagonal of the adopted packet form directly, rather than treating $b^*b$ as an unbounded operator on an unspecified domain or extending [F2]'s vector theorem by assertion.

Operator-norm convergence in [A2] implies $|B_{\ell,s}(f,f)-B_{\ell,\infty}(f,f)|\le\|B_{\ell,s}-B_{\ell,\infty}\|\|f\|_2^2\to0$; using $\|f\|_2=1$ and the value computed in step 1.1 proves the finite-packet limit.

Set $g(\omega)=\Gamma_\ell(\omega)n_\theta(\omega)$ and $d\mu_\epsilon=|f_\epsilon(\omega)|^2d\omega$. The common band $K$ is compact and bounded away from zero, and [F3] gives $n_\theta(\omega)>0$ there; with the postulated continuous $\Gamma_\ell$, $g$ is bounded and continuous on $K$. For any $\eta>0$, continuity gives a neighborhood $V$ of $\omega_0$ in $K$ on which $|g(\omega)-g(\omega_0)|<\eta$. Choose a continuous $q:K\to[0,1]$ with $q(\omega_0)=0$ and $q=1$ outside $V$. Weak convergence $\mu_\epsilon\rightharpoonup\delta_{\omega_0}$ gives $\int q\,d\mu_\epsilon\to0$, hence $\mu_\epsilon(K\setminus V)\to0$. Therefore $\left|\int_Kg\,d\mu_\epsilon-g(\omega_0)\right|\le\eta+2\|g\|_\infty\mu_\epsilon(K\setminus V)\to\eta$; as $\eta$ is arbitrary, the integral tends to $g(\omega_0)$.

Apply step 2.1 at each fixed $\epsilon$, then step 2.2 to the resulting spectral integral. This order yields $\Gamma_\ell(\omega_0)/(e^{2\pi\omega_0/k}-1)$ and does not replace a finite-width integral by its central-frequency value.

By the definition of $T_\infty$ in the Statement, $\theta\omega=\hbar\omega/(k_BT_\infty)$ for every $\omega>0$; solving $\theta=2\pi/k$ gives $T_\infty=\hbar k/(2\pi k_B)$. Substituting the model value $k=c^3/(4GM)$ from [F4] gives $T_\infty=\hbar c^3/(8\pi GMk_B)$. Its units are $(\mathrm{J\,s})(\mathrm{s^{-1}})/(\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}})=\mathrm K$. The conclusion is a model-derived spectral parameter and contains no observed temperature.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Put $\theta:=2\pi/k$ seconds and $n_\theta(\omega):=(e^{\theta\omega}-1)^{-1}$. Define the incoming number form on $\mathcal H_K\oplus\mathcal H_K$ by
$$q_{\ell,K}((f_1,f_2),(g_1,g_2)):=\int_K\overline{f_1(\omega)}g_1(\omega)n_\theta(\omega)\,d\omega,$$
where the first component is the near-horizon signal and the second is the independent incoming vacuum channel. Define the packet map induced by the first row of the passive mode transformation by
$$J_{\ell,K}f:=\bigl(\sqrt{\Gamma_\ell}\,f,\sqrt{1-\Gamma_\ell}\,f\bigr).$$
The exact limiting form is the adopted direct-integral model input
$$B_{\ell,\infty}(f,g):=q_{\ell,K}(J_{\ell,K}f,J_{\ell,K}g)=\int_K\overline{f(\omega)}g(\omega)\Gamma_\ell(\omega)n_\theta(\omega)\,d\omega.$$
Thus the signal has the exponential-channel occupation $n_\theta$, the environment and signal-environment cross terms vanish by the incoming vacuum and independence premises, and the passive map supplies the transmission factor. Assume that for each fixed $K$ the bounded forms converge in operator norm as $s\to+\infty$ to this $B_{\ell,\infty}$, meaning
$$\sup_{\|f\|_2,\|g\|_2\le1}|B_{\ell,s}(f,g)-B_{\ell,\infty}(f,g)|\longrightarrow0.$$
